summary:
Public Law 118–230, the Accelerating Appraisals and Conservation Efforts Act (AACE Act), establishes a single-state licensure rule for real property appraisers performing services for transactions over which the Secretary of the Interior has jurisdiction. The Act adds a new section, 43 U.S.C. § 1478, which provides that a covered appraiser—defined as a State-licensed or -certified real property appraiser—need be licensed or certified in only one State to perform appraisal or valuation services in any State for such a transaction (subsection (a)).

Subsection (b) directs that, when the Secretary uses a non-Federal covered appraiser, the Secretary shall, to the maximum extent practicable, use a certified general real property appraiser licensed in the State where the property is located, and may use an appraiser licensed in another State only upon a determination that a local appraiser is unavailable, not assignment-qualified, or not cost competitive.

Subsection (c) requires the Secretary to submit a report to Congress not later than one year after the January 4, 2025, date of enactment and annually for at least four years thereafter. The report must include: a quantitative comparison of the number of appraisal requests received and completion times before and after enactment; a qualitative assessment of the flexibility afforded by subsection (a); recommendations for congressional action to improve efficiency while preserving independence, impartiality, and objectivity; an overview of the Department’s appraisal workforce; and a complete list of cases where the authority under section 2 was used, describing the specific criteria applied.

Subsection (d) contains three statutory clarifications: (1) except as provided in paragraph (3), nothing in the section affects the application of any Federal or State law or regulation to a non-Federal covered appraiser; (2) the section does not authorize performance of services in a State where the appraiser is not licensed except for covered transactions; and (3) any pre-enactment Federal or State law or regulation requiring a covered appraiser to be licensed in a specific State does not apply to transactions within the Secretary’s jurisdiction, thereby preempting conflicting state licensing requirements for these transactions.

Subsection (e) imposes a 90-day deadline after enactment for the Secretary to make publicly available online and upon request all policies, manuals, guidance documents, handbooks, standard operating procedures, and policy statements regarding the scoping, contracting, and review of appraisals performed by Federal or non-Federal covered appraisers. The Act contains no authorization of appropriations.
